newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa says under cartel office probe.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa says under cartel office probe.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Monday it was being probed by the German cartel office over its pricing structure on domestic routes.
A spokesman for the airline said in response to a Reuter query: "I can confirm that the investigation is going on. We cannot comment further on a running procedure."

The Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung reported on Monday that Lufthansa's Frankfurt-Berlin route, costing 800 marks ($540) in business class, had provoked cartel authorities to ask the airline to disclose its pricing structure after "various complaints."
The paper said Lufthansa's business class travel between Cologne or Duesseldorf to Berlin, routes also flown by a unit of British Airways, cost only 640 marks.
Lufthsansa's spokesman added: "We cannot operate without covering our costs. Nobody can force any company to set prices that do not cover costs."
